definitions.gloss: giant tree; great tree; large old tree
definitions.explanation: An exceptionally large tree, often old and revered. In Japan, giant trees are sometimes designated as natural monuments.

examples.japanese: {森|もり}の{奥|おく}に{巨木|きょぼく}がそびえている。
examples.english: A giant tree towers deep in the forest.

examples.japanese: この{巨木|きょぼく}は{樹齢|じゅれい}{千年|せんねん}を{超|こ}えると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: This giant tree is said to be over a thousand years old.

examples.japanese: {屋久島|やくしま}の{縄文杉|じょうもんすぎ}は{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{有名|ゆうめい}な{巨木|きょぼく}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: The Jomon cedar on Yakushima is one of the most famous giant trees in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
Often associated with nature worship and spirituality. In Japan, particularly large or old trees at shrines are sometimes wrapped with {注連縄|しめなわ} (sacred rope) and revered as sacred. The word carries a sense of awe and majesty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巨木|きょぼく}がそびえる (a giant tree towers)
- {巨木|きょぼく}の{森|もり} (a forest of giant trees)
- {天然記念物|てんねんきねんぶつ}の{巨木|きょぼく} (a giant tree designated as a natural monument)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大木|たいぼく}: large tree — similar but slightly less dramatic
- {古木|こぼく}: old tree — emphasizes age rather than size
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}: sacred tree — a tree revered at a shrine
